Extract an array of subject specific parameters from a fit

Source: R/summary.ctStanFit.R
ctSubjectPars.Rd

Extract an array of subject specific parameters from a fit from ctFit, on either backend. ctStanSubjectPars is maintained as a backward-compatible alias.

Usage

ctSubjectPars(
  fit,
  pointest = TRUE,
  cores = getOption("mc.cores", 2L),
  nsamples = "all",
  level = NULL,
  uncertainty = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

A fit from ctFit.

pointest

if TRUE, returns only the set of individual difference parameters based on the max a posteriori estimate (or the median if sampling approaches were used).

cores

Number of cores to use. backend='stan' only, and an error for a julia fit, which already holds the subject matrices.

nsamples

Number of samples to calculate parameters for. Not used if pointest=TRUE.

level

For a model with nested ids (id = c('person', 'couple') in ctModel), the level to report. The default is the subject level (the first id). A grouping level above it gives each group's own parameter values, which are the population values shifted by that group's random effects and those of the levels above it, without subject level effects or TI predictor effects. Grouping levels need a backend='julia' fit, and their draws follow uncertainty as for subjects.

uncertainty

For backend='julia' fits with pointest=FALSE, what the draws include. 'total' (the default) pairs each draw of the population parameters with a draw of each subject's random effects from their posterior given that subject's data. The spread then includes both the uncertainty of the population parameters and how well the subject's own data determine its parameters. 'conditional' keeps the population parameters at the estimate and draws only the subject's effects. 'population' varies only the population parameters, with each subject at its estimate, which understates a subject's uncertainty when its own data are weak. A fit that sampled its random effects (optimize=FALSE) only supports 'total'.

Value

an nsamples by nsubjects by nparams array, with the subjects (or groups, for a grouping level) labelled by their ids in the data.

Details

This function returns the estimates of individual parameters, taking into account any covariates and random effects, at every level of a nested model.

A julia fit also stores, for every level with random effects, each group's posterior for its effects on the raw parameter scale, in fit$randomeffects: one entry per level, with each group's mean deviation from the population value and its covariance packed column by column (cov). The draws with uncertainty='total' come from this posterior.

Examples

indpars <- ctSubjectPars(ctstantestfit)
dimnames(indpars)
plot(indpars[1,,'cint1'],indpars[1,,'cint2'])
